content: 1. The elimination half-life of azelastine is approximately 25 hours, while its active metabolite, desmethylazelastine, has a longer elimination half-life of about 57 hours. 2. Following oral administration of radiolabeled azelastine hydrochloride, approximately 75% of the dose is excreted in the feces, with less than 10% being excreted as unchanged azelastine. 3. In patients with hepatic impairment, pharmacokinetic parameters of azelastine were not significantly affected following oral administration. 4. In individuals with renal impairment (creatinine clearance <50 mL/min), single-dose oral studies showed a 70-75% increase in both maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) and area under the curve (AUC) compared to healthy subjects. However, the time to reach maximum concentration (Tmax) remained unchanged. 5. Age does not influence the pharmacokinetic parameters of azelastine following oral administration. 6. Gender does not affect the pharmacokinetic parameters of azelastine following oral administration. 7. The effect of race on the pharmacokinetics of azelastine has not been evaluated. 8. Co-administration of azelastine (4 mg twice daily) with erythromycin (500 mg three times daily for 7 days) resulted in a Cmax of 5.36 ± 2.6 ng/mL and an AUC of 49.7 ± 24 ng·h/mL for azelastine. When azelastine was administered alone, the Cmax was 5.57 ± 2.7 ng/mL, and the AUC was 48.4 ± 24 ng·h/mL. 9. In a multiple-dose, steady-state drug interaction study, cimetidine (400 mg twice daily) increased the mean oral azelastine concentration (4 mg twice daily) by approximately 65%. 10. Co-administration of azelastine (4 mg twice daily) with ranitidine hydrochloride (150 mg twice daily) resulted in a Cmax of 8.89 ± 3.28 ng/mL and an AUC of 88.22 ± 40.43 ng·h/mL for azelastine. When azelastine was administered alone, the Cmax was 7.83 ± 4.06 ng/mL, and the AUC was 80.09 ± 43.55 ng·h/mL. 11. No significant pharmacokinetic interaction was observed when azelastine hydrochloride (4 mg twice daily) was co-administered with theophylline (300 mg or 400 mg twice daily). 12. In 2-year carcinogenicity studies in rats and mice, azelastine hydrochloride did not demonstrate evidence of carcinogenicity at oral doses up to 30 mg/kg and 25 mg/kg, respectively. These doses correspond to approximately 150 and 60 times the maximum recommended human daily intranasal dose (MRHDID) on a mg/m² basis. 13. Azelastine hydrochloride showed no genotoxic effects in various tests, including the Ames test, DNA repair test, mouse lymphoma forward mutation assay, mouse micronucleus test, and chromosomal aberration test in rat bone marrow. 14. Reproductive and fertility studies in rats showed no adverse effects on male or female fertility at oral doses up to 30 mg/kg (approximately 150 times the MRHDID in adults on a mg/m² basis). However, at a dose of 68.6 mg/kg (approximately 340 times the MRHDID on a mg/m² basis), there was a prolongation of estrous cycles, reduced copulatory activity, and decreased numbers of pregnancies. The numbers of corpora lutea and implantations were also reduced, although pre-implantation loss was not increased. 15. The efficacy and safety of azelastine hydrochloride nasal solution (nasal spray), 0.1% with sweetener, were evaluated in a 2-week, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial involving 834 patients aged 12 years and older with symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis. 16. Patients were randomized into six treatment groups, receiving either one or two sprays per nostril of azelastine hydrochloride nasal solution (with or without sweetener) or vehicle placebo, administered twice daily. 17. Efficacy was assessed using the 12-hour reflective total nasal symptom score (rTNSS), which evaluates four individual nasal symptoms (rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, sneezing, and nasal itching) on a 0 to 3 severity scale. The rTNSS required patients to record symptom severity over the previous 12 hours. 18. For the primary efficacy endpoint, the mean change from baseline in rTNSS was calculated by summing the morning (AM) and evening (PM) scores for each day (maximum score of 24) and averaging over the 2-week period. 19. Azelastine hydrochloride nasal solution (0.1% with sweetener) administered as two sprays per nostril twice daily demonstrated a statistically significant greater reduction in rTNSS and iTNSS compared to placebo. 20. The efficacy of azelastine hydrochloride nasal solution (0.1% with sweetener) administered as one spray per nostril twice daily for seasonal allergic rhinitis was supported by two 2-week, placebo-controlled clinical trials involving 413 patients. 21. In these trials, azelastine hydrochloride nasal solution (without sweetener) demonstrated a statistically significant greater reduction in the summed AM and PM rTNSS compared to placebo. 22. The efficacy and safety of azelastine hydrochloride nasal solution (0.15% with sweetener) for seasonal allergic rhinitis were evaluated in five randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials involving 2,499 patients aged 12 years and older. 23. The primary efficacy endpoint in these trials was the mean change from baseline in rTNSS over 2 weeks. 24. Two 2-week trials evaluated the efficacy of azelastine hydrochloride nasal solution (0.15% with sweetener) dosed at two sprays per nostril twice daily. 25. In these trials, azelastine hydrochloride nasal solution (0.15% with sweetener) demonstrated statistically significant greater reductions in rTNSS compared to placebo.
